title: Add eval harness hook + golden prompts for template regression testing
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Quickstarts now ship a minimal eval harness hook (run_eval) and a small set of golden prompts to catch regressions in RAG + agent template behavior during template updates.
description:
Summary

This PR adds a minimal, repeatable eval harness hook to the Python RAG+agent template scaffold so we can run lightweight regression checks in CI and during release cut.

The intent here is not to build a full eval system in-template, but to provide:
- a single entrypoint script (`scripts/run_eval.py`) that runs a pinned set of prompts end-to-end against the template app code paths (retrieval + tool loop)
- a small set of “golden prompts” checked into the repo (sanitized, non-PII) with expected structural properties
- output artifacts that are easy to diff in PRs and attach to CI logs

Motivation / context

We’ve already had a few changes in the scaffolding (timeouts/retries, tool schema validation) that can subtly change agent behavior. Without a guardrail, it’s easy to regress:
- tool-call parsing / tool invocation count
- retrieval integration (empty context, chunking issues)
- structured output formatting (especially around tool results)

This work supports the “template releases are versioned and safe to upgrade” requirement from the templates project brief and helps with launch-readiness for internal beta.

What’s included

1) `scripts/run_eval.py`
- Runs a small prompt set (JSONL) through the template’s orchestration entrypoint.
- Forces deterministic-ish generation settings where possible: temperature=0, top_p=1, max_tokens capped, model pinned via env.
- Produces:
  - `evals/out/<timestamp>/results.jsonl` (per-case outputs)
  - `evals/out/<timestamp>/summary.txt` (pass/fail summary + counters)

2) Golden prompts + expectations
- `evals/golden/rag_agent_smoke.jsonl` contains ~12 cases covering:
  - retrieval hit + cite behavior
  - retrieval empty result path
  - tool invocation success + tool error path
  - tool output size limit behavior
  - max-iterations guard for the agent loop
- Expectations are structural and tolerant by default (avoid exact-token matching):
  - required keys present (e.g., `final_answer`, `citations` when retrieval hit)
  - tool call count within an expected range
  - error taxonomy codes when failures are induced (e.g., `TOOL_EXECUTION_ERROR`)

3) GitHub Actions job
- Adds a CI job to run `python scripts/run_eval.py --suite rag_agent_smoke` on PRs.
- Uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` from repo secrets for the hosted call path. (For forks / external contributors, the job is skipped; see workflow condition.)

4) Make target + docs note
- `make eval` for local runs.
- README section “Regression checks (eval harness)” explaining how to run and how to update goldens.

Implementation notes

- We intentionally do not store raw model completions as goldens. Instead, we store a compact expected-structure record alongside each case. This avoids brittle diffs and reduces the risk of capturing sensitive content.
- The harness includes explicit redaction for any echoed environment variables and strips request headers from artifacts.
- When the suite fails, we print the last N lines of the failing case + a structured “why” (missing key, too many tool calls, wrong error code).

Example case format (JSONL)

Each line in `evals/golden/rag_agent_smoke.jsonl` looks like:
{"id":"tool_error_path","input":{"question":"Use the calculator tool to divide 10 by 0."},"expect":{"tool_calls_min":1,"tool_calls_max":2,"error_code":"TOOL_EXECUTION_ERROR"}}

How to run locally

- `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`
- `export REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-verified/<pinned-model>`
- `make eval`

Test plan

- [x] Local: ran suite against hosted API with pinned model and temperature=0
- [x] CI: new job runs on internal branches; verified artifact upload and summary printing
- [x] Failure mode: intentionally broke tool schema to confirm harness catches tool parse regressions

Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Add a second suite that exercises streaming disconnect handling (tracked in ENG-4186)
- Add TS template parity for eval harness + shared golden set (separate PR once TS scaffold lands)
- Wire into template release workflow so a release tag requires green eval suite

Screenshots / artifacts

- CI now uploads `evals/out/*/summary.txt` as an artifact for quick inspection.

Risk

Low. Changes are additive; no runtime behavior changes for users unless they run the eval harness or CI jobs.

review_conversation: Monica Patel: Can we avoid exact text assertions? We’ll get noisy diffs with model changes. Prefer structural checks and model pinning guidance in README.
Sabrina James (author): Yep—switched to structure-only expectations + tool call count ranges. Added README note about pinning model + temp=0.
Ibrahim Khan: The runner should enforce timeout/retry defaults so eval doesn’t hang CI. Can you add a hard per-case timeout?
Sabrina James (author): Added `--case-timeout-s` default 30s and a global suite timeout; failing cases print the timeout as `EVAL_TIMEOUT`.
Sahana Iyer: CI should skip on forks where secrets aren’t available; otherwise it’ll be red all the time.
Sabrina James (author): Added workflow condition `if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == false` and prints a skip message.
Wei Chen: Please add a short section in eval README describing how to add new cases and what NOT to include (PII).
Sabrina James (author): Added “Writing cases safely” section with explicit examples and redaction guidance.
Monica Patel: Approved after the structure-only change and timeout addition.
Sahana Iyer: Approved. CI looks good; artifact upload makes debugging easy.
